notes:
Units that speak KWP2000 over ISO 15765-2 on the 500 kbit/s diagnostic CAN ('IS' in arduino-psa-diag). Peugeot, Citroen, DS and Opel or Vauxhall cars on PSA platforms (the sources name no brand, so brand coverage is by platform and unconfirmed). Every row is unconfirmed until `obd-read probe` shows the unit answering on a car.

Architecture and pins: AEE2004 and AEE2010 cars carry diagnostics on OBD pins 3 (CAN high) and 8 (CAN low), not the socket's usual pins 6 and 14, so an ELM327 or STN adapter needs a pass-through adapter or cable that routes pins 3 and 8 to its CAN input (arduino-psa-diag README 'PINOUT'; PyPSADiag README 'Use of ELM327 Support'). NEA2020 cars are the other way round: the arduino-psa-diag README says the original pins 6 and 14 are used for DoIP (diagnostics over IP), while the PyPSADiag README says NEA2020 cars have the diagnostic CAN on pins 6 and 14 and need no adapter. The two sources disagree and neither was tested here (issue 38 tracks settling it). One source (PyPSADiag README) advises a branded adapter with a genuine MAC address rather than a clone, since a poor one often cannot read zones at all.

Bit rate: the profile uses 500 kbit/s, which the arduino-psa-diag sketch sets for the diagnostic CAN bus (CAN_SPEED CAN_500KBPS, 'Diagnostic CAN bus - High Speed') and a ServiceBox forum post gives for the diagnostic CAN on pins 3 and 8. The same post says ServiceBox shows the vehicle's CAN IS on pins 6 and 14 at 250 kbit/s but measured 500 kbit/s there. The sketch repository also ships a separate low-speed sketch at 125 kbit/s for the entertainment bus. No source opened gives 250 kbit/s for the diagnostic CAN itself, so only the bus on pins 6 and 14 has two reported values.

ID sharing: several families share one request and response pair, so one row stands for every family listed in its description and the row's name is the first family's name in the table, not a claim about the unit. The unit behind a row is read from its identification, never inferred from the ID. A response identifier is not always the request minus 0x100, so both are recorded.

Pairs the table gives to two different units cannot sit in one profile (a reply must be attributable), so the first pair in this order keeps its identifiers: a pair PyPSADiag lists, then a pair whose response is the request minus 0x100 or 0x20, then table order. The losers are listed in docs/vehicles/europe-other.md. LIN-attached units are reached through a LIN selector (L47, L48, L68, L70) that this tool cannot send, so a row whose table entry carries one reaches only the gateway unit.

Protocol: PyPSADiag lists one ECU model on a 500 kbit/s KWP2000 link (the DAE_BVH2 file of the DIRECTN family on 6B5:695). Every other row is a pair no source gives a protocol for, so it appears here and in psa-uds; a unit that does not answer here is probably UDS. The 'HAB' KWP2000 variant (125 kbit/s, session 0xC0) is not covered: the guard's read-only list allows only sessions 0x81 and 0x92, and the 125 kbit/s bus is not the diagnostic CAN. Pairs PyPSADiag lists only as HAB (airbag 744:644, radio 760:660, amplifier 77D:67D, BECB 6C4:604) are therefore in neither profile.
